key_insight: Paired transition-metal dopants are more stable than isolated dopants and offer a route to tunable, high-temperature ferromagnetism in 2D MoSe₂ and WSe₂.
engineering_relevance: Dopant-cluster engineering could enable atomically thin magnetic semiconductors for room-temperature nano-spintronic devices.
method: DFT+U calculations of dopant stability and magnetic properties.
Analysis of exchange coupling, spin–orbit coupling, and orbital hybridization.
Monte Carlo estimation of Curie temperature.
evidence_signal: Calculations predict long-range ferromagnetic coupling for all studied paired dopants in MoSe₂, in-plane MAE values of −3.5 meV for paired V in MoSe₂ and −3.2 meV for paired Mn in WSe₂, and a Curie temperature near 440 K for paired Fe in MoSe₂.
watch_item: These computational predictions require experimental validation, particularly controlled dopant-pair formation and magnetic stability in fabricated monolayers.
paper_title: Dopant Cluster Engineering for Tunable Room-Temperature Ferromagnetism in 2D Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
